pages.desc: YSKAR is a proof-of-work currency with a blockchain of its own. Nothing was handed out in advance: every YSR is mined, and anyone can check every block.
Taking part in YSKAR costs nothing: create a wallet, mine with a phone or a PC, run a node or simply watch the chain. Pick the way in that suits you.
New YSR come from mining and from nowhere else. Mine with a phone, a PC or a graphics card, alone or in a pool. With a calculator based on live chain data.
YSKAR Wallet is the Android app for YSR: send, receive, sign. Your key is created on your phone and stays there. No ads, no tracking, no account.
A full node checks every block itself, from block 0, and passes it on. Run YSKAR Node Core on Windows or Linux and help keep the network hard to bend.
YSR is the coin of the YSKAR chain. There will never be more than 21,000,000, and nothing was pre-mined or allocated: every YSR comes from a found block.
YSKAR runs on a chain of its own: its own blocks, its own peer-to-peer network and its own rules, proven with work that anyone can check.
What the YSKAR chain is doing right now, read from the public API: block height, hashrate, nodes, block times and who found the latest blocks.
Look up a YSKAR block, a transfer or an address. Your browser recomputes the proof of work of every block it shows.
All of YSKAR is open source under the MIT License: node, wallets, miners, explorer and website. A public API answers without a key.
YSKAR is a community project and belongs to the people who use it. This is where they talk, test and decide.
Where YSKAR comes from, what runs today and what comes next. Changes take effect at a block, not on a calendar day.
Step by step: mining on the phone and on the PC, your wallet, your own node and your own pool.
The YSKAR protocol in detail: coin, chain and wallets in one datasheet, the 136-byte block header, the transfer format and block 0.
The YSKAR whitepaper: blocks, transactions, proof of work, difficulty, issuance, wallets, pool mining and the network.
